subject: SIG: Clarification on Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC/on-prem) responsibilities
messages:
From: Samantha Price <samantha.price@acme.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up - need clarification on hosting modes and responsibilities

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our InfoSec team is working through the SIG questionnaire and we hit a few items where we need a concise explanation of how Redwood's deployment modes differ for control ownership and evidence. Specifically:

- For Hosted: we need to confirm who controls keys, where logs live, and what evidence we can provide for segregation and PII handling.
- For Dedicated: clarify what is tenant-isolated vs shared infra, and whether we can get per-tenant audit logs and network diagrams.
- For Private (VPC / on-prem): we need to understand what Redwood still operates vs what the customer is responsible for (KMS, backups, OS patching), and sample evidence for on-prem installs.

Can you provide a short narrative we can paste into the SIG answers and point us to supporting artifacts? If you have a one-page matrix or diagram, that would help.

We are aiming to finish SIG round 1 by end of next week.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Price
Senior Security Engineer, Acme Corp

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@acme.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up - need clarification on hosting modes and responsibilities

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick reply with a high-level narrative and attachments; happy to expand any line into explicit SIG question/answer pairs. Attached: a one-page explainer and a KMS integration diagram.

High-level (paste-friendly):

- Hosted (Redwood API): Redwood operates the serving control plane and runtime in our managed cloud. Customer data is logically isolated per account; keys are managed by Redwood KMS by default. Option: customer-managed keys (CMKs) for enterprise customers via Cloud KMS/HSM integrations. Audit logs (access, admin, model actions) are retained in Redwood's logging stack and can be exported to customer destinations (S3/Cloud Storage) under contractual terms. Evidence: SOC 2 report, network diagram showing multi-tenant logical isolation, sample audit log extract.

- Dedicated (Reserved Capacity): Dedicated GPU pools reserved for the customer. The runtime and GPU hosts are dedicated but some control-plane services (scheduling, monitoring) remain in Redwood-managed control plane unless customer subscribes to private control plane. Customers get per-tenant audit logs and can enable stricter network isolation (VPC peering, private endpoints). Keys: CMK supported; logs: per-tenant export. Evidence: topology diagram for dedicated pools, per-tenant logging sample, SLA and contract excerpt.

- Private (VPC / On-prem): Customer-managed compute and networking. Redwood provides a private control plane and deployment packages; customer operates infrastructure (or we operate under an MSA with defined ops scope). Responsibilities shift: customer handles host OS patching, local backups, and network perimeter; Redwood provides runtime updates, deployment artifacts, documented hardening steps, and optional remote support. KMS/HSM integration is customer-side; we support bring-your-own-KMS and provide guidance for key rotation and audit. Evidence: deployment checklist, deployment acceptance test logs, HSM integration guide.

If you want, we can convert each bullet into explicit SIG answers (Q: Who is responsible for X? A: Redwood/Customer) and attach a drafted spreadsheet you can drop into the SIG portal.

Attaching: deployment-mode-explainer.pdf, redwood-kms-integration-diagram.png

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachments: deployment-mode-explainer.pdf (pdf), redwood-kms-integration-diagram.png (image)

Jonas, thanks for the helpful overview. A couple of follow-ups from our compliance team:

1) For Private/VPC: can you confirm where audit logs are stored by default and whether we can require logs be written to our controlled bucket? We need evidence for the SIG that logs are retained for at least 90 days and that tamper-evidence is applied.
2) For Dedicated: when you say "per-tenant logs," are these logically separated files in the same centralized store or physically segregated? Example we need: a sample log file header showing tenant ID and timestamp.
3) For Hosted CMK option: do you support hardware-backed keys (HSM) and are you able to provide an attestation/certified HSM vendor name for SIG?

Also, we noticed the Hosted description implies Redwood may export logs to customer destinations "under contractual terms" — can you point to the contractual clause or sample addendum?

If you can include the specific SIG QIDs we should place these answers under, that would speed review.

Best,
Acme Security Team

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com

Hi Samantha / Acme team —

Below are concrete, SIG-ready answers and references. I've attached a draft SIG responses spreadsheet (sig-responses-draft.xlsx) with QID mapping. Please review and let me know if you want any wording tightened for legal.

1) Private / VPC (logs & tamper-evidence)
- Default: when deployed as Private (customer VPC or on-prem), audit logs are written to the customer-managed storage endpoint you configure (we do not retain a separate copy unless explicitly contracted). This satisfies customer-controlled retention and avoids Redwood-managed retention by default.
- Tamper evidence: we provide SHA256-signed log bundles at configurable intervals and a sequence + checksum manifest you can fetch; instructions and sample manifests are in the attached deployment guide.
- SIG reference: map answers to SIG QIDs: LOG-01 (collection), LOG-02 (retention), LOG-07 (integrity controls).

2) Dedicated (per-tenant logs)
- Separation: logs are written with tenant identifiers in dedicated prefixes/keys in our centralized object store (log-shipping to per-tenant prefixes). They are logically segregated; for Dedicated with a private control plane we can arrange physical segregation on request — we note that physical segregation requires an addendum and may affect lead times.
- Example evidence: sample log header (attached as plain-text extract in the spreadsheet) showing tenant_id, request_id, and ISO8601 timestamp.
- SIG mapping: LOG-03 (tenant separation), LOG-05 (exportability).

3) Hosted CMK & HSM
- We support customer-managed keys via integrations with major cloud KMS providers and allow HSM-backed CMKs (Cloud HSM / KMS-backed HSM). Vendors commonly used by customers: AWS CloudHSM, Google Cloud HSM, Azure Key Vault (HSM).
- Evidence: we can provide a statement of support and a sample integration diagram (redwood-kms-integration-diagram.png). For HSM attestation, we rely on the cloud provider attestation (we can provide provider documentation references).
- SIG mapping: CRYPT-01 (key ownership), CRYPT-04 (HSM support).

4) Contractual clause for log export
- Clause: Data Export & Logging Addendum (sample clause included in the draft MSA Addenda doc we can share). For SIG convenience, see related link to our contract FAQ in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/redwood/internal/deployment-modes (link provided).

Next steps: I'll drop the sig-responses-draft.xlsx into the Drive folder and can turn each line into the SIG portal copy if you provide the QIDs you want us to target. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min call to walk through the drafted answers and attachments.

Thanks — copying our solutions lead for Dedicated/private packaging.

Jonas Weber
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
